complete_selected_source_lines.complete_line: Seia arrives seeking proof that she can stand without prophecy. The event makes that wish both valuable and mistaken when it becomes the belief that needing help invalidates her. Nagisa’s care, Rio’s rationalized protection and Seia’s effort all have real reasons, but none gives one person unrestricted authority over another’s participation. Neru articulates limits directly, Karin asks for information, and Seia learns through seeing Rio demand the same impossible self-proof. Ordinary pleasure and company—not merely useful institutional service—are the wish that the ending tries to make possible. Its success is bounded: Rio agrees to stay a week; neither the whole week nor full legal/technical accountability is narrated.

The final invitation is a mixture of wanted company and useful pretext. Seia asks Rio to stay another week and witness the event she protected. Rio denies qualification to enjoy it. Seia argues that EXPO is only at its first day, Seminar may not resolve every later exception and Rio can help. Neru adds that staying discreetly might be a president’s job; this is a suggestion, not a new installed office state. Rio feels she is being persuaded. Neru says no one can force her if she dislikes it; she says she has not said she dislikes it, agrees to one week and goes to unpack. Her explicit limit—leave when the event ends—remains. No later safe week, cure, public absolution or permanent return is established.
